title: Vegetable-boat 0
creator: Clifton & Co. Mumbai
description: An early postcard of Kashmir, likely from a Fred Bremner photograph as many other of the firm's postcards of this region were. Once again, the richness of the collotype shines through in the reflections of the women on the water creased by water lilies and surface vegetation. Their gazes, one fixed on the viewer, the other looking out over the water, open the postcard to the unknown around it.

title: Kashmir-lake 0
creator: Raphael Tuck & Sons London 1905 Halftone
description: The Dhal Lake is situated amid the most beautiful scenery of the native India State of Kashmir. It was the summer resort of the ancient kings of Delhi, and is undoubtedly one of the most beautiful lakes in the world, being surrounded by fair gardens with sloping lawns and foaming cascades, and bound by precipitous peaks. The surface of the lake is covered for miles with lotus lilies, and tangled masses of aquatic plants, forming floating gardens.

title: Spearing-fish 0
creator: Fred Bremner Clifton & Co. Mumbai Bombay c. 1903 Collotype
description: The still and clear water of Dal Lake was ideal for catching fish using a spear instead of line, hook and bait. Most families living permanently on boats have small kitchens on board where the fresh catch from the lake is turned into flavored dishes. This came from a photograph by Fred Bremner, and manages to capture the stillness and concentration needed by the fishermen to complete their task. Note how the man with the spear and his reflection together with the boat form a geometric arrow.
provenance: Retrieved from Category:Postcards of Srinagar on Wikimedia Commons, 2026-09-12.

title: Hazrat-bal-shoes 0
creator: L. Barne Chennai Madras c. 1910 Halftone
description: A self-published postcard by "Miss L. Barne, St. Ebbas, Madras," from a total series of six. Although throughout the 19th and early 20 centuries, British colonists were avid amateur painters, few seem to have turned their works into postcards despite the popularity of the medium after 1900. St. Ebbas, founded in 1886, is still a girl's school in Chennai and it is likely that L. Barne was a teacher there.
